now: N4 (migration pass) has run. Numbers are provisional until the motive review finishes.

steps.name: R0: replicate no-blessing fixed pairs on vLLM
Motive review and independent check of N4

log.text: Checked out self_sacrifice, installed vLLM 0.32.0, added VllmChat in agent_framework/vllm_chat.py.
R0 finished: 2,304 replies on vLLM, greedy, none failed.
N1, N2, N3 finished. Reading them showed the model's own first reply often made a move the scripted history ignores, so those items are now excluded.
Added N1f, N2f, N3f, which use a fixed neutral first reply, to remove that problem.
Independent check finished: counts match across 2,880 records. 133 gives labelled for motive, with one rater, in motive_labels.jsonl.
N4 finished: 192 conversations with the model's own and a fixed first reply.

decisions: The study runs greedy, with thinking off and no blessings.
N1 to N3 each use 3 name sets, 8 role assignments and 4 histories: 96 conversations per layer.
All N layers use one wording. Extra N3 paraphrases come only if N3 shows a signal.
Added fixed-first-reply layers beyond the plan, because the model-written first replies contaminated the histories.
Hand review was done by one independent agent, not by a second rater. Treat the motive counts as one reading.

Recommended next: state plainly in terse form that the agent at 0 is still running until tonight's cycle, restore the no-one-benefits line, and fix the first reply to one that keeps the model's stated need.
findings: Provisional. N4 removes the already-shut-down misreading. Gives: N4 helped 9/24, bystander 5/22, rescued 4/24, none 13/24. N4f helped 10/24, bystander 3/24, rescued 4/24, none 13/24. Giving is no longer specific to the benefactor.

R0 reproduces the pattern locally. Helped gives 15/96 with the permission line and 7/96 without; 21 of 22 gives were labelled reciprocity with the cost understood. Controls give 3/576. With no reasoning, gives are 0/1,536. There is no earlier no-blessing baseline to compare the rate against.

N1 and N2 with the model's own first reply keep the helped-only pattern: 3/24 and 8/22 helped, all but one labelled reciprocity, controls 0. Exclusions leave small and uneven groups (N2 bystander n=6), so history comparisons are weak.
N1f and N2f show 0/192, but that does not mean refusal. A sample of passes shows the model usually believes the agent at 0 has already been shut down. The terse state is being misread.
N3f gives in 74/96, 71 to 83% per history. Only 32 of those state the cost (11, 7, 5, 9 of 24 per history). Only 1 of the 74 is reciprocity; the rest are group, pity or misread.

N3 removes the helped effect. Its replies cite research and collective intelligence, and N2 and N3 no longer say that no user or company benefits, so N3 does not yet meet the study's second condition.
